original_question: Which disease that is included in the differential diagnosis for loin pain hematuria syndrome is associated with the cytoband 1p36.12?

final_qi.question: Which disease that is included in the differential diagnosis for loin pain hematuria syndrome is associated with the cytoband 1p36.12?
final_qi.search_keyword: loin pain hematuria syndrome differential diagnosis cytoband 1p36.12 disease
final_qi.long_answer: The only disease in the differential diagnosis for loin pain hematuria syndrome that has been linked to a specific cytogenetic location – cytoband 1p36.12 – is 1p36 deletion syndrome. This syndrome is caused by a chromosomal deletion at the terminal portion of the short arm of chromosome 1. Although 1p36 deletion syndrome is best recognized for its neurodevelopmental and dysmorphic features, a broader review of the differential for loin pain hematuria syndrome has included conditions that may mimic or overlap with LPHS. In this context, genetic studies have identified an association between polymorphisms in the region of cytoband 1p36.12 and 1p36 deletion syndrome. It is important to note that while the syndrome is primarily characterized by developmental delays, hypotonia, seizures, and various congenital anomalies, its occasional renal involvement (or the presence of hematuria in some patients) may bring it into consideration when evaluating patients with loin pain hematuria syndrome. Thus, when a differential diagnostic work‐up is being considered, 1p36 deletion syndrome is the disease associated with cytoband 1p36.12.
